newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-George Weston says trading on budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-George Weston says trading on budget.

text.p: George Weston Foods Ltd said on Tuesday the company was trading in line with its budget estimates, despite a flat retail market, and planned to pay a special A$1.00 fully-franked dividend.
Shareholders would vote on the special dividend in January.
"The group overall is trading in line with budget despite a flat retail market," chief executive and deputy chairman John Pascoe told the company's annual meeting.

"Directors have recogised the company's improved results and its strong financial position and intend to resolve, subject to shareholder approval and the necessary administrative and regulatory requirements to pay a special fully franked dividend equivalent to A$1.00 per share from the company's franking credit account," Pascoe said.
The company also intended to introduce a dividend reinvestment plan and boonus share plan for the purposes of the special dividend.

George Weston, is about 78 percent owned by Associated British Foods Plc, reported a net profit of A$24.95 million for the six months to January 31, compared with A$22.87 million for the previous corresponding period.
